chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

Bundar, the freedman of Idris, wrote: 'O our master, I vowed to fast every Saturday. If I do not fast it, what expiation (kaffarah) will be incumbent upon me?' He (peace be upon him) wrote back and I read it: 'Do not leave it, except due to an excuse. And you are not required to fast it during travel or illness, unless you intended that. And if you broke it without an excuse, then give charity for the count of each day to seven poor people. We ask Allah for success in what He loves and is pleased with.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking a vow to fast on a specific day without a valid excuse?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Hasan al-Saffar, clarifies the binding nature of a specific vow to fast on Saturdays, distinguishing between general exemptions for travel and illness versus those explicitly intended. It establishes a precise expiation (kaffarah) of feeding seven poor people for each missed day if the fast is broken without a valid excuse, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on fulfilling personal vows (nadhr) with specific compensatory measures. The ruling underscores the importance of intentionality in religious obligations and the practical application of fidya in cases of unintentional or excused non-performance.
